title: Sand Timer Race

serves.summary: The child flips sand timers to time animals and a tower-builder, then shows which was done first, which took longer, or how many timers a long walk needed.

request.topic: Timing activities with a sand timer
request.objective: Use a sand timer to compare how long two simple activities take, and predict whether an activity will finish before the sand runs out.

problems.ask: Does the frog get to its lily pad before the sand runs out? Put the flag on the one that was done first.
problems.goal: The frog's three slow hops take longer than one sand timer, so the sand runs out first: the flag goes on the sand timer.

problems.ask: Each frog has its own sand timer. Which frog took longer to reach its lily pad?
problems.goal: The big frog goes further in three quick hops; the little frog's six small hops take longer, and its timer has less sand left. The ribbon goes on the little frog.

problems.ask: Building a tall tower, or the snail crawling to the leaf: which will take longer? Put the ribbon on your guess, then time them both.
problems.goal: Ten blocks go up fast; the snail's short crawl is slow. The ribbon ends on the snail, placed before timing and kept after.

problems.ask: The bunny goes first, then the bird has a turn. Which one took longer?
problems.goal: The bird starts second and finishes last, but its own timer shows it took less time: more sand is left. The ribbon goes on the bunny.
